```java
75 :     int    CHKSUMLEN = 8;
```"

Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The failing test `testCOMPRESS335()` attempts to load a problematic TAR archive ("COMPRESS-335.tar") that has a checksum stored with zero padding on the left instead of the standard null or space padding on the right side of the checksum field.

The core of the issue lies in the `TarUtils.verifyCheckSum(byte[] header)` method. This method reads the 8-byte checksum field starting at offset 148 (`CHKSUM_OFFSET = 148`) for length 8 (`CHKSUMLEN = 8`). The current logic reads the checksum as up to 6 octal digits (0 to 7) left-to-right, incrementing `digits` counter, multiplying the stored sum by 8 each time and adding the digit value. If any character is outside '0'-'7' or once more than 6 digits are read, digits counting stops. The rest of the checksum bytes are replaced by ASCII space (0x20) when calculating the signed and unsigned checksum sums.

The validation then compares the parsed stored checksum to either an unsigned or signed sum of the entire header bytes (after substituting the 8 checksum bytes with spaces).

The bug occurs because the TAR files with left-padded zeros in the checksum field have their meaningful octal digits shifted to the right, which means the current code only considers the leftmost up to 6 octal digits starting from position 148. The last two digits are ignored if right-aligned and zeros come first.

This results in an incorrect `storedSum` that misses those trailing digits and thus triggers checksum verification failure, despite the rest of the header being valid and the last two checksum digits being correct but ignored.

The recent bug report describing similar issues with checksum handling confirms this. The report suggests that since the code already checks that digits are in '0'-'7' octal range before adding, the logic could be changed to parse all 6 octal digits regardless of position to properly handle right-aligned zero-padding.

In summary, the checksum parsing logic in `TarUtils.verifyCheckSum` incorrectly restricts itself to reading only the first 6 valid octal digits left-to-right in the 8-byte checksum field. It cannot handle checksums that are right-aligned with padding zeros on the left, causing valid TAR files to fail verification.

This diagnosis aligns with the failing test, which tries to parse such a TAR file and fails because the checksum is found invalid due to this logic.

The recent bug report about "Some non TAR files recognized..." also points out the nuances in checksum validation, reinforcing the complexity of correct checksum verification handling.

Hence, the root cause is the limited left-to-right parsing of up to 6 octal digits in the checksum field that ignores trailing digits if the checksum is right-aligned with zeros on the left.

The fix would involve changing the parsing method to correctly parse all relevant octal digits in the checksum field irrespective of their position within the 8 bytes, possibly by trimming zero-padding or adjusting the digits counting logic.

---
